chapter: Recent years and early piano influences
title: Sheet-music piano solos: Confrey, Alter, Rube Bloom
summary: Publishers issued piano solos by pianist-composers like Zez Confrey, Louis Alter and Rube Bloom.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: When were you first conscious of Earl Hines then?
Well, there was a composer... Usually in those days the sheet music had piano solos; you know, Zes(?) Coffrey.
Oh yes. That was sort of "Intermezzo" time.
I think that's what they called it.
He was sort of flashy, a flash-in-the-pan, and he... Another one also, Louis Alter, who wrote "Manhattan Serenade." Then there was also (?)Rube Bloom(?). I was very impressed. He did "Sapphire"...

"Soliloquy." And these... It was a very... It was quite a business. Publishers used to put out these various booklets and sheet music. For instance, if there was a popular song, you know, like a (?), they would put it out not only in sheet music form for the vocal, but also different, various pianists, the way they would play it. Well, Rube Bloom(?) was one of them with piano solos... They were very interesting. And of course, at that time, I just couldn't find one that has this "57 Varieties". Man, that's rough!
